mainTopic: How בית שמאי treat a שומרת יום כנגד יום, the argument over watching after bleeding on the tenth day, and whether the eleven days of זיבה are a הלכה למשה מסיני or come from פסוקים.
overview: The amud first finishes a challenge to רב הונא. He said that for בית שמאי, a שומרת יום כנגד יום who immersed and had relations is definitely טמאה by rabbinic law. A ברייתא seems to show that בית שמאי treat her only as תולין (in suspense). The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as talking about the man who was with her, not the woman herself. It then explains that the רבנן decreed only for common cases. A second challenge comes from the משנה, which says her contact is 'suspended.' The גמרא answers that this clause follows only בית הלל, using a ברייתא of רבי יהודה whose wording it corrects. Next, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether bleeding on the tenth day of the eleven זיבה days needs watching. Each one ties his view to how he reads the הלכה למשה מסיני about the eleven days. Finally the גמרא asks whether the eleven days really come from פסוקים, and begins quoting a ברייתא to show this. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about moving a first-sighting discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If someone moves the discharge from a man's first sighting of זוב, בית שמאי say his purity is held in suspense, and בית הלל say he is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a ברייתא teaches: if someone moves the discharge, בית שמאי say his status is held in suspense, and בית הלל say he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for a challenge against רב הונא. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who sees זוב once is not yet a full זב. בית שמאי say we wait and see: if he sees again, the first discharge counts as זוב, and whoever moved it becomes טמא. בית הלל say one sighting is just like an ordinary emission, so moving it does not make a person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who moves something without touching it (היסט), which can pass on טומאה
A 'sighting,' meaning a discharge that was seen
Held in suspense: the status depends on what happens later
They rule it pure

steps.confusionAlert: תולין does not mean 'impure.' It means we do not know yet. The final status depends on whether a second sighting comes.

phrases.english: And it is taught: one who moves the discharge that was seen
phrases.notes: This means the discharge from the man's first sighting of זוב, before we know if he is a full זב.

steps.title: Beds and seats between the first and second sighting
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: items for lying and sitting that the man used between his first and second sighting are in suspense for בית שמאי and pure for בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Beds and seats used between the first sighting and the second sighting: בית שמאי say they are held in suspense, and בית הלל say they are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes on with a second case that follows the same pattern, still setting up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full זב makes the things he lies or sits on טמא. Since we do not yet know if this man is a זב, בית שמאי keep those items in suspense until we see whether a second sighting comes. בית הלל treat them as pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Items made for lying and sitting, which a זב can make טמא
The first sighting

steps.title: The opening clause compares him to a שומרת יום כנגד יום
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of the ברייתא says בית שמאי compare this man to a שומרת יום כנגד יום. Since his status is תולין, it seems a שומרת יום כנגד יום is also only תולין for בית שמאי. That contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the first clause teaches: one who sees one sighting of זוב, בית שמאי say he is like a שומרת יום כנגד יום. So it seems that for בית שמאי, a שומרת יום כנגד יום is held in suspense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts the pieces together and makes the challenge clear. רב הונא said בית שמאי hold a שומרת יום כנגד יום is definitely טמאה, but this ברייתא implies she is only in suspense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the man is 'like' a שומרת יום כנגד יום. It also rules that, for בית שמאי, his status is תולין. If he is like her, her status must also be תולין, and that goes against רב הונא, who said she is definitely טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a source
An abnormal discharge that can make a man a זב
A woman who saw blood in her זיבה days and must watch for a clean day for each day she saw
Apparently, this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: The whole challenge depends on the word 'like': if the man is like the שומרת יום כנגד יום, then they should share the same status.

phrases.english: And it teaches in the first clause:
one who sees one sighting of zov,
Beit Shammai say:
he is like a woman who watches a day for a day.
Apparently, a woman who watches a day for a day
according to Beit Shammai, is held in suspense.
phrases.notes: This is the problem: רב הונא had said בית שמאי hold she is definitely טמאה, not just in suspense.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Joins the first clause of the ברייתא to the rulings already quoted, which turns them into a challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that בית שמאי hold a שומרת יום כנגד יום is definitely טמאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא compares the man to a שומרת יום כנגד יום and rules his status is תולין. That implies her status is also תולין.

steps.title: Read it as 'like the man who had relations with her'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. The man is compared to someone who had relations with a שומרת יום כנגד יום, not to the woman herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not say 'like a שומרת יום כנגד יום.' Rather, say 'like one who has relations with a שומרת יום כנגד יום.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב הונא by changing whom the man is being compared to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The status of the man who had relations with her depends on whether she sees blood later in the day, so his status is תולין. The woman herself can still be definitely טמאה, just as רב הונא said. So the ruling of תולין in the ברייתא now fits רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this; rather, say that. This rereads the wording of a source.
A man who has relations with a woman

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's view survives: for בית שמאי, the woman is definitely טמאה, while the man who had relations with her is only תולין.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the גמרא is saying the woman is תולין. Only the man who had relations with her is in suspense.

phrases.english: Do not say 'a woman who watches a day for a day,'
rather, say

phrases.notes: Whether he becomes טמא depends on whether she sees blood later that day, so his status really is 'in suspense.'

steps.title: Why is she stricter than him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the בועל of a שומרת יום כנגד יום does not definitely make משכב ומושב impure, while she herself does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference? He does not make items for lying and sitting impure, but she does make them impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the answer from step 4. Why are the man and the woman treated differently?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the man in the ברייתא is like a בועל of a שומרת יום כנגד יום, and his status is only תולין. But according to רב הונא, the woman herself is definitely טמאה and makes משכב ומושב impure. So the גמרא asks why there is a gap between them.

Items made for lying and sitting, which become impure when a זב or נדה lies or sits on them

phrases.notes: "Him" is the man who had relations with a שומרת יום כנגד יום, from step 4.

steps.title: Blood is common for her, so the רבנן made a decree
steps.stepSummary: Blood is not common for him, so the רבנן did not decree. Blood is common for her, so they did decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is someone for whom blood is not common, so the רבנן did not make a decree about him. She is someone for whom blood is common, so the רבנן made a decree about her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A woman often sees blood, so the רבנן were strict with her. A man does not, so they were not strict with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her strict status is a גזירה (a rabbinic decree), based on the idea that she may well see blood again. The man's impurity would only come indirectly through her. Since he is not someone who regularly sees blood, the רבנן did not extend the decree to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Are common, happen often
Blood, meaning sightings of blood
The רבנן made a decree (a rabbinic safeguard)

phrases.english: He, for whom blood is not common,
the רבנן did not make a decree about him;
she, for whom blood is common,
the רבנן made a decree about her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree applies to her because she often sees blood. It does not apply to him because he does not.

steps.title: Then why doesn't she make the man impure?
steps.stepSummary: If there is a decree on her, why does she make משכב ומושב impure but not the בועל?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about lying and sitting, that she makes them impure, and what is different about the man who was with her, that she does not make him impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second follow-up question. If the רבנן decreed that she is טמאה, why doesn't her impurity pass definitely to the man?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said the decree is on her. If so, her impurity should spread to everything she makes impure, including the בועל. Yet her bedding and seats are definitely impure, while the man is only תולין. The גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who has relations with her

phrases.english: And what is different about lying and sitting

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב דִּמְטַמְּיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 6 and asks why the decree on her does not reach the בועל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why her decreed impurity spreads to משכב ומושב but not to the man who was with her.

steps.title: Lying and sitting are common, relations are not
steps.stepSummary: Lying and sitting happen constantly, so they are included in the decree. Relations happen less often, so they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Lying and sitting, which are common, she makes impure. The man who is with her, which is not common, she does not make impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the decree only covers things that happen all the time. That closes this discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן usually make decrees for situations that come up often. She lies and sits on things constantly, so those items were included in the decree. Relations with a שומרת יום כנגד יום are much less frequent, so the רבנן did not decree on the בועל, and he stays only תולין.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not common, does not happen often
She does not make impure

steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, a שומרת יום כנגד יום is definitely טמאה and makes משכב ומושב impure, because blood is common for her and lying and sitting are common. The man who was with her is only תולין, because the רבנן did not decree on uncommon cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule that the רבנן make decrees mainly for common situations. That is how the ברייתא and רב הונא's view can fit together.

phrases.english: Lying and sitting, which are common,
she makes them impure;

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁכָּב וּמוֹשָׁב דִּשְׁכִיחַ מְטַמְּיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree covers common situations like lying and sitting, but not relations, which are uncommon.

steps.title: A challenge from the משנה: her contact is only 'suspended'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a woman who immersed the day after seeing blood and then had relations has done wayward conduct, and her contact and relations are 'suspended.' It asks whether this is everyone's view, which would contradict רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: If she immersed on the day after, and had relations, this is wayward conduct. Their touching and their relations are suspended. Isn't this the view of everyone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to challenge רב הונא. The משנה says the impurity status of what she touched is left in doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Suspended' means we wait to see: if she sees blood again, she is a זבה and everything is impure; if not, it is pure. If both בית שמאי and בית הלל agree, then even בית שמאי treat her items as only doubtful, which does not fit רב הונא's statement.

The day after she saw blood
Wayward, improper conduct
What they touched and their relations
Suspended; left in doubt until we see what happens
The view of everyone, here both בית שמאי and בית הלל

steps.confusionAlert: 'Suspended' does not mean definitely impure or definitely pure. It means the answer depends on whether she sees blood again later that day.

steps.title: This part of the משנה is only בית הלל, with a ברייתא as support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 'suspended' clause is only the view of בית הלל. It brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה addresses בית הלל about calling this case wayward conduct.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is בית הלל. As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה said to בית הלל: Do you call this wayward conduct? He only intended to have relations with a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה here follows בית הלל alone, so it says nothing about בית שמאי. It supports this with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה argues with בית הלל about calling this case 'wayward conduct.' That shows the phrase in the משנה comes from בית הלל, so רב הונא's view of בית שמאי is not contradicted.

steps.title: Could it really mean a נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא: the case is not about a נדה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could you really think it means a נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask about רבי יהודה's words. The woman in this case is not a נדה, so the wording cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה and ברייתא are talking about a woman watching a clean day after seeing blood, not a נדה. So 'a נדה' must be reread.

steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches the woman in the משנה, who immersed the day after seeing blood. Now the ברייתא clearly speaks about this case and is addressed to בית הלל, which supports the answer that the 'suspended' clause is בית הלל's view.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: ״לִבְעוֹל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם״.
phrases.english: Rather, say: to have relations with a woman who watches a day for a day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: לִבְעוֹל שׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final reading after step 13 rejected 'זבה.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says נדה or זבה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a שומרת יום כנגד יום, matching the case in the משנה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the tenth day is like the ninth
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a woman who bleeds on the tenth day of the eleven days must watch the next day, just as she must after bleeding on the ninth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated about the tenth day: רבי יוחנן said the tenth day is like the ninth. Just as the ninth day needs watching, so too the tenth day needs watching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an argument about a woman who bleeds on the tenth of the eleven days of זיבה. It starts with רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she bleeds on the ninth day, she might also bleed on days 10 and 11 and become a זבה גדולה, so she must watch the next day. רבי יוחנן treats the tenth day the same way: it is still a day of זיבה, so she must watch the following day.

keyTerms.meaning: Watching: the woman must check that the next day is clean of bleeding (שומרת יום כנגד יום)
The tenth day of the eleven days of זיבה
The ninth day of the eleven days of זיבה

phrases.english: It was stated: the tenth day,
phrases.notes: The tenth of the eleven days between one נדה period and the next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: the tenth is like the ninth,
just as the ninth requires watching —
so too the tenth requires watching.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: עֲשִׂירִי, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion after the ברייתא wording was settled in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding on the tenth day requires watching the next day, just like the ninth.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the tenth day is like the eleventh
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that bleeding on the tenth day does not require watching, just like the eleventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said the tenth day is like the eleventh. Just as the eleventh day does not need watching, so too the tenth day does not need watching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing view: ריש לקיש says the tenth day does not need watching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she bleeds on day 10, three days in a row would be days 10, 11 and 12. Day 12 already starts her נדה period, so she cannot complete three days of זיבה and become a זבה גדולה. That is why ריש לקיש compares day 10 to day 11, when no watching is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The eleventh, last day of the זיבה window
Does not require

steps.confusionAlert: Watching here is about whether she could become a זבה גדולה (three days in a row). Day 10 is still a day of זיבה. ריש לקיש only says it works like day 11 when it comes to watching.

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: עֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַד עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: the tenth is like the eleventh,

phrases.aramaic: מָה אַחַד עָשָׂר לָא בָּעֵי שִׁימּוּר —
phrases.english: just as the eleventh does not require watching —
so too the tenth does not require watching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: עֲשִׂירִי כְּאַחַד עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite ruling to רבי יוחנן's view in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding on the tenth day does not require watching, like the eleventh day.

steps.title: Another version: the eleven days are a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the argument as tied to a ברייתא in which רבי אלעזר בן עזריה tells רבי עקיבא that the eleven days, along with two other measures, are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this argument on the following source. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to רבי עקיבא: Even if you keep learning from the word 'in oil' all day long, I won't listen to you. Rather, half a לוג of oil for the תודה, a רביעית of wine for the נזיר, and the eleven days between one נדה period and the next are all a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש was taught. It quotes the ברייתא first, to set up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא tried to learn the half לוג of oil from the repeated word 'בשמן' in the פסוק. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects that and says these measures are not learned from פסוקים at all. They are a tradition handed down from סיני, and that includes the eleven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Some teach it on this source instead (a second version)
A law handed down orally from משה at סיני, not learned from a פסוק
The thanks offering
A quarter of a לוג
A person who took a vow to avoid wine and more

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the eleven-day window of זיבה rests on a tradition from סיני, not on a פסוק. The next step asks what exactly that tradition says.

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on this:
phrases.notes: "It" is the argument between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to Rabbi Akiva:
Even if you amplify 'in oil,' 'in oil,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12. The second 'בשמן' in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ, אֵינִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לְךָ!
phrases.english: the whole day long, I will not listen to you!
Rather, half a log of oil for the thanks offering,
and a quarter-log of wine for the nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם שֶׁבֵּין נִדָּה לְנִדָּה —
phrases.english: and the eleven days between menstruation and menstruation —
are a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the source the argument in steps 15-16 was taught on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Half a לוג of oil for the תודה, a רביעית of wine for the נזיר, and the eleven days between נדה periods are all הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: What exactly is the הלכה about the eleven days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the הלכה למשה מסיני about the eleven days actually teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the eleven days are a הלכה, but it does not spell out which rule is included. The answers will show where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: What?

phrases.english: What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הֲלָכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of 'הלכה' in the ברייתא from step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What rule about the eleven days the הלכה למשה מסיני includes.

steps.title: One rule or several rules for the eleventh day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it is one rule about the eleventh day. ריש לקיש says it is rules (plural) about the eleventh day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the rule of the eleventh day. ריש לקיש says: the rules of the eleventh day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the two answers. They match each sage's earlier view about the tenth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says one rule: only day 11 is special and does not need watching, so day 10 still does. ריש לקיש says 'rules,' plural: more than one day near the end gets this special treatment, so day 10 also does not need watching.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule of (singular)
The rules of (plural)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: day 10 needs watching like day 9 (one special rule, for day 11). ריש לקיש: day 10 does not need watching, like day 11 (special rules cover both).
steps.confusionAlert: The whole argument rests on one letter: singular הלכת against plural הלכות. Read the two words carefully.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הִלְכַת אַחַד עָשָׂר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: the law of the eleventh,

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: הִלְכוֹת אַחַד עָשָׂר.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish says: the laws of the eleventh.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: הִלְכַת אַחַד עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 18 with two views.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן: a single rule, for the eleventh day only. ריש לקיש: rules (plural), which also cover the tenth day.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: one rule, only the eleventh day is free from watching
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains the singular הלכה. Only the eleventh day needs no שימור. All the other days, including the tenth, do need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the one rule about the eleventh is that the eleventh day is the day that does not need watching. For the other days, she does watch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out exactly what רבי יוחנן's one rule (הלכת, singular) about the eleventh day says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The tradition from סיני only exempted the eleventh day from שימור. Every earlier day, including the tenth, keeps the normal rule that she must watch the next day. This is the source for רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: The rule of (singular): one law
Watching: checking that the next day is clean of blood
Here: the eleventh day, the last day of the זיבה window
The others: here, the other days

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says:
The rule (singular) of the eleventh:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַד עָשָׂר הוּא דְּלָא בָּעֵי שִׁימּוּר,
phrases.english: it is the eleventh that does not require watching,
but for the others, she does watching.
phrases.notes: "The others" includes the tenth day. That is why רבי יוחנן says bleeding on the tenth needs watching.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי יוחנן אמר הלכת אחד עשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the content of רבי יוחנן's 'one rule' from step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the הלכה of the eleven days teaches
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only the eleventh day is exempt from שימור; the other days, including the tenth, require it

steps.title: ריש לקיש: two rules, so the tenth day also needs no watching
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains the plural הלכות. The eleventh day needs no שימור. It also cannot count as the שימור day for the tenth, so the tenth needs no watching either.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: the rules about the eleventh are that the eleventh does not need watching, and it is also not a watching day for the tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out ריש לקיש's two rules (הלכות, plural) about the eleventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second rule is the key. Watching for the tenth day would have to happen on the eleventh. Since the eleventh cannot be used as a watching day, the tenth ends up needing no watching. This explains ריש לקיש's ruling in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The rules of (plural): more than one law
The tenth day
Is / serves as

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש never says outright that 'the tenth needs no watching.' He says the eleventh is not a watching day for the tenth, and that is how the tenth ends up exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads one rule from סיני, so the tenth still needs watching. ריש לקיש reads two rules, so the tenth does not need watching.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish says:
The rules (plural) of the eleventh:
neither does the eleventh require watching,
nor is it a watching day for the tenth.
phrases.notes: Since the eleventh can't be used to watch for the tenth, the tenth day needs no watching at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וריש לקיש אמר הלכות אחד עשר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading, next to רבי יוחנן's
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the הלכות of the eleven days teach
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The eleventh needs no שימור and cannot serve as שימור for the tenth

steps.title: Are these really laws from סיני? They come from פסוקים!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's claim that the eleven days are a הלכה למשה מסיני, because they seem to be learned from פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these laws given orally at Sinai? They are learned from verses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the eleven days are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני is a rule with no source in the written תורה. If the eleven days can be learned from פסוקים, calling them a tradition from סיני makes no sense. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: laws passed down orally from Sinai
Verses of the תורה
Are they?

phrases.english: Are these laws from Sinai?
These are verses!

steps.triggerLanguage: הני הלכות נינהו הני קראי נינהו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and questions its basic claim
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement that the eleven days are a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something learned from a פסוק cannot also be called an oral law from Sinai

steps.title: A ברייתא's first guess: three days at the start makes her a זבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the eleven days come from פסוקים. The ברייתא opens with a first guess that three straight days of bleeding at the start of the נדה days would make her a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: One might think that a woman who sees blood three days in a row at the start of her נדה days becomes a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא as proof. The ברייתא opens with a first guess that it will later reject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יכול' signals a first guess that the ברייתא will reject with a פסוק. The ברייתא is building toward showing from the פסוקים that the נדה days and the זבה days are separate. That is the eleven-day system.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think: a first guess that will be rejected
A woman with an irregular flow, who counts seven clean days and brings a קרבן
In a row, one after another
The start of the נדה days

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One might think that one who sees blood three days
in a row at the start of the נדה days
will be a זבה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דתניא יכול הרואה שלשה ימים בתחילת נדה רצופים תהא זבה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim that the eleven days come from פסוקים
steps.raayaObject: That the נדה/זבה days are learned from פסוקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that works this out from the פסוקים

steps.title: The ברייתא applies the פסוק to one day of bleeding and moves to its proof פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא keeps up its first guess. It reads the נדה verse as talking about a woman who sees for only one day. Then it starts to bring the פסוק that will reject this guess.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do I explain 'If a woman has a flow, and her flow be blood'? It speaks of one who sees for one day. (But one who sees for three days at the start would be a זבה.) The verse says:
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא defends its first guess by explaining the נדה verse. Then it sets up the פסוק that will knock the guess down. That פסוק comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the first guess, the נדה verse would only cover a one-day sighting, and three days would make her a זבה. 'תלמוד לומר' signals that a פסוק is about to prove otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: How do I explain this verse? (according to the first guess)
Her flow
The verse teaches: brings a פסוק as proof

phrases.english: And how do I explain
"If a woman has a flow,
and her flow be blood"?
It speaks of one who sees for one day,
(but one who sees for three days
at the start will be a זבה),
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. They just repeat the first guess.

phrases.english: The verse says:

steps.triggerLanguage: ומה אני מקיים אשה כי תהיה זבה דם יהיה זובה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's first guess and sets up its rejection
steps.raayaObject: That the נדה/זבה days are learned from פסוקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's reading of ויקרא 15:19 and the פסוק that follows
